High-density housing could be on the way for the inner north, Planning Minister Chris Steel has announced.

Login or signup to continue reading

A major plan amendment to allow for higher-density development between Dickson and Civic will be released for public consultation in the first quarter of 2027, Mr Steel said at the Property Council's Capital Region Housing Summit on November 17.

Mr Steel said the amendment would complement the existing draft major amendment proposing similar changes in Downer and Watson.

It would allow for higher-density housing in Dickson, where development has largely been restricted to Northbourne Avenue and the group centre.

The new amendment would focus on enabling more housing to be built in the "transition zone within walking distance of light rail stops," Mr Steel said.

"This will ensure that the territory plan properly reflects the long-term housing needs of the city, close to the city," he said.

The Dickson section of Northbourne Avenue has undergone a substantial facelift over the past decade, with the social housing blocks torn down on either side of the avenue to make way for new, high-density apartment buildings.

Construction on Art Group's Soho Precinct, on the eastern side of the road, was finished earlier this year. On the western side of the road, the final residential stage of JWLand's "Northbourne Village" has also been completed.

Geocon is currently building a two-building apartment complex on the corner of Northbourne and Wakefield avenues. Development in the inner parts of the suburb has been more limited.

"While some developers have proposed spot rezoning on the other sites close to the city, we've heard clearly from members of the community and from the legislative assembly that they have a preference for zoning changes to be progressed in a way which presents a broader spatial vision for urban densification in the city," Mr Steel said.

To facilitate the densification of the inner north, Mr Steel also announced a review of the controversial lease variation charge, which applies when the approved uses of land under a Crown lease are changed.
